title: Open normal subgroups form an identity neighbourhood basis in a profinite group
statement: Let $G$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group: multiplication and inversion are continuous, and every connected subset of $G$ has at most one point. Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For every open subset $U\subseteq G$ containing the identity $1$, there exists an open normal subgroup $H\leq G$ such that $H\subseteq U$. Here normal means $gHg^{-1}=H$ for every $g\in G$.
